claims.text: A high-thermal-conductivity underlayer beneath the FeMnNiGeSi film or nanoribbon will improve interfacial heat extraction.
Improved interfacial heat extraction will sharpen the magnetocaloric transition.
Improved interfacial heat extraction will reduce hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons have intrinsic microstructural disorder.
Interfacial effects are pronounced in the nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
A copper or high-conductivity ceramic underlayer is the proposed controlled intervention.
The underlayer will enhance thermal transport across the film/substrate boundary.
The enhanced thermal boundary will minimize thermal lag and interfacial temperature gradients.
Thermal diffusion is rate-limiting during the specified magnetic-cooling cycles.
Reducing thermal lag lowers the contribution of diffusion-limited magnetic disorder.
Underlayer-equipped samples will have a narrower magnetic hysteresis loop than otherwise identical as-deposited controls.
Underlayer-equipped samples will exhibit a sharper magnetocaloric entropy-change feature than otherwise identical as-deposited controls.
As-deposited controls without thermal-boundary engineering have broadened magnetic transitions because of limited heat transfer.
As-deposited controls have increased hysteresis because of limited heat transfer.
The proposed effect applies at low magnetic fields and cycle frequencies for which thermal diffusion is rate-limiting.
Previous observations in similar systems support the proposed benefit of enhanced thermal management.
